transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Dr. Nina (Acme ML), Samir (Acme Platform), Lydia (Acme Security)

Summary (auto): POC scoping to determine deployment mode for Acme Biotech: aim is to validate latency and throughput on realistic workload, plus confirm security posture for sensitive genomic data. Discussed success criteria, workload sizing, bench plans, and timeline.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'm jordan with redwood inference, and with me is priya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
00:06 Dr. Nina: good hey thanks for setting this up, excited — we want to figure this out pretty quickly. we have regulatory constraints so security is big for us.
00:12 Priya: great thanks, can you kick off with a quick overview of the workload? what's the main latency/throughput you care about and what does a successful pilot look like?
00:20 Dr. Nina: sure. at a high level we run genomic variant annotation queries. the typical request is a short prompt — like a VCF snippet plus context — and the model returns an annotated interpretation. average request size is ~350 tokens, but the critical calls are short ~50-100 tokens for real-time interactive tools. For success criteria we want p50 latency under 200 ms for the short interactive calls, p95 under 600 ms; throughput target is ~100 qps sustained during daytime hours, burst to 300 qps tolerable. Accuracy/quality metrics will be defined by a set of golden prompts, we need no regression from our baseline. Also data residency in EU and audit logs are mandatory.
00:54 Samir: also worth noting we have a multi-tenant platform, but we can dedicate a namespace. we currently run pre- and post-processing on k8s in our GCP project. we care about predictable cost per inference — surprises are hard to manage.
01:06 Jordan: that's super helpful — yeah so the decisions are typically between hosted, dedicated, and private. hosted is fastest to stand up, great for trying benchmarks quickly; dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput/costs; private (VPC or on-prem) is for strict compliance and data residency.
01:20 Lydia: for us, private is attractive because of patient data, but private deployments add ops overhead. curious how much work it is to push the POC on hosted first then migrate.
01:30 Priya: absolutely — common pattern is start with hosted for benchmarking with customer-provided sample payloads and then if you hit security/regulatory blockers, move to Dedicated or Private. we can run a hosted benchmark using dedicated test instances we spin up for the POC.
01:42 Dr. Nina: i like that. what about latency differences between modes — do you have ballpark numbers?
01:47 Priya: ballpark: hosted (our multi-tenant) typically has slightly higher variance because of shared pools but p50 can be 50–150ms for short calls depending on model choice and quantization; dedicated is tuned for lower variance and better p95 since you get reserved capacity and specific kernel/runtime settings; private depends on customer infra — if on-prem GPUs are modern and well-configured you can match or beat dedicated, but infra tuning is on you. caching (prefix/KV cache) and batching are big levers.
02:11 Samir: we have Nvidia H100s on prem but smaller cluster; for initial POC i'd prefer hosted to move quickly, but will need a plan if the firewall/audit folks push back.
02:20 Jordan: for the POC we usually define: 1) success criteria (latency, throughput, quality), 2) workload sizing (qps, token distribution, burst patterns), 3) benchmark plan (prompts, datasets, metrics), 4) timeline and gating criteria for migration to dedicated/private.
02:34 Dr. Nina: let's walk through each — success criteria: p50 < 200ms for short calls, p95 < 600ms, throughput 100 qps sustained, handle 300 qps bursts for up to 5 minutes. and quality must be within 2% accuracy of our current model on golden set. Also need audit logs and SSO.
02:52 Priya: noted. on workload sizing can you send us a 7-day traffic histogram and the top 1k prompts? that lets us simulate realistic batching/cache behavior and pick model variant and quantization profile.
03:02 Samir: yes we can do that, i'll export from our metrics tomorrow.
03:05 Lydia: on security: we need SOC2 + HIPAA summary, SSO via SAML, customer-managed KMS for private mode, and optionally bring-your-own-key for dedicated. will the hosted option support BYOK?
03:18 Jordan: BYOK for hosted is limited — we offer managed KMS for hosted, but dedicated and private support integration with customer KMS/HSM. for hosted we can provide encryption at rest and in transit, and we have SOC2 docs. i'll attach the security pack.
03:31 Dr. Nina: also latency vs cost — we need a cost estimate for each mode for the expected qps. can you provide per-token and reserved capacity pricing?
03:39 Jordan: yes, we will provide an estimate. hosted per-token pricing, dedicated reserved monthly pricing with utilization assumptions, and a rough on-premia estimate for private (license + support). priya will run a cost model during the benchmark to estimate per-inference cost given token distribution.
03:51 Priya: for the benchmark itself we recommend starting with a hosted run using a small dedicated test pool: steps
   - customer shares 1k sample prompts + 7-day traffic pattern
   - we run generation workload on 2 model variants (int8 quantized and fp16) and measure p50/p95, throughput, GPU utl, token/sec and cost
   - run a stability test for 2 hours at 100 qps and a 10 minute burst at 300 qps
   - capture traces and KV cache hit rates

04:27 Dr. Nina: sounds good. for privacy we'd prefer not to send PHI to third party, so could we obfuscate or synthetic-ize samples?
04:33 Jordan: yes, synthetic or redacted prompts work fine, the perf characteristics (token lengths, prompt shapes) are what matter. if you need us to run within EU only, we can ensure data stays in EU-hosted instances.
04:45 Samir: timeline wise we want to start asap. what's a realistic schedule for a POC and then a decision?
04:52 Priya: POC schedule we suggest: week 0 (this week): gather artifacts; week 1: hosted benchmark runs and initial results; week 2: iterate on perf tuning and run stability tests; week 3: review results and cost model; 4–6: if moving to dedicated, provision reserved capacity and run migration tests; private/on-prem will need more lead time for infra and network setup (4–8 weeks depending on approvals).
05:16 Lydia: that's reasonable. what about rollbacks and fallbacks if dedicated capacity is constrained?
05:20 Jordan: we support automated fallback policies — you can route to compatible model variants or lower-cost zones; the console supports route policies by latency or cost. we can demo that in the follow-up.
05:31 Dr. Nina: any gotchas on model versioning or prompt changes during the POC?
05:35 Priya: we recommend pinning a model version for benchmarks; we also record evals on prompt sets to detect regressions. if you change prompt templates, we re-run small eval slices.
05:44 Samir: ok last thing — can you show rough numbers for expected GPU usage for our workload? 100 qps with average 350 tokens — ballpark.
05:52 Priya: rough calc: token/sec = 100 qps * 350 tokens = 35k tokens/sec. depending on model size and quant, that could be a couple of H100s sustained for generation-heavy models, but with batching and KV cache we often drop effective throughput needs. we'll give a more precise estimate once we get the top-1k prompts and token distribution.
06:12 Jordan: great — i'll send the security pack and pricing and priya will follow up with the benchmark harness.
06:18 Dr. Nina: perfect, we'll get sample prompts and traffic patterns over by monday, and lydia will send the security constraints.
06:24 Jordan: perfect thanks everyone. recap: send security docs, share prompts, schedule hosted benchmark week of 2026-03-15, follow-up 2026-03-22 to review.
06:33 Samir: thanks all, bye.
06:35 Lydia: thanks, bye.
